text: Zollo and colleagues propose jointly optimizing an acceptance model and a recalibrator so that the retained region is easier to calibrate. This is a candidate design for an abstaining signal system, not a demonstrated five-minute SOL result. (low confidence)

text: Probability calibration and useful abstention are distinct objectives. text: A risk-coverage curve evaluates selection by pairing the error or loss among accepted predictions with the fraction of predictions accepted. It answers a different question from whether a reported probability matches an observed frequency. (low confidence)

text: Farinhas and colleagues propose non-exchangeable conformal risk control for the expected value of monotone losses. The framework weights observations by relevance to a test example. text: Selective prediction evaluates a predictor together with an acceptance rule. Coverage is the probability of acceptance; selective risk is expected loss conditional on acceptance. For a five-minute signal, using these as an evaluation framework is a proposed application, not evidence of trading performance. (low confidence)

text: Calibration quality and selective accuracy are separate objectives. Zhu and colleagues report that many calibration methods worsen error detection in their experiments; Zollo and colleagues note that enforcing selective calibration can decrease accuracy. text: The Zhou–Wang audit conditions its selective-risk certificate on exchangeable calibration and test points. text: Methodological inference from conditional selective risk: evaluate net outcomes within the accepted population and report acceptance coverage. An average over all observation times alone does not determine the selected subset’s mean, so it cannot by itself rule out or establish the profitability of a rare-trigger policy. This is a distinction between conditional and unconditional evaluation, not a claim that any SOL policy is profitable. (low confidence)

text: Zollo and colleagues state that selective calibration is not monotonic as individual examples are removed, and that a mismatch between training and deployment coverage can hurt test performance. A stricter acceptance threshold should therefore be evaluated at its actual coverage rather than assumed to improve calibration. (low confidence)

text: Selective calibration evaluates whether predicted probabilities match outcome frequencies within the accepted subset. Fisch and colleagues train a separate selector for this objective; their author implementation describes the same accepted-population target. For the proposed signal gate, this motivates checking calibration after acceptance as well as before it. (medium confidence)

text: Adaptive conformal inference targets prediction-set coverage frequency over long time intervals under changing distributions. text: CAP constructs a calibration set using an adaptive pick on historical observations after a current observation is selected. Its dynamic extension targets long-run false coverage-statement rate, the overall miscoverage level of reported prediction intervals. (low confidence)
